Low severity per the scan (foreign student ids aren't enumerable through RLS) but confirmed. Two further findings from the same re-scan (both verdict:plausible, not confirmed -- EmergencyContact creation in ContactosEmergencia.jsx not verifying parent-student linkage, SupportTicketMessage creation in tickets.js not verifying ticket ownership) plus one rls_recommendations entry (tighten UserProfile.create/update to admin-only) were deliberately NOT fixed this pass -- each needs its own guarded backend function or an onboarding-flow audit, out of scope for a same-day follow-up. previousBumpRationale_1_7_5: Patch, critical security fix: completing 1.7.3's module-4 live deploy (base44/entities/*.jsonc → the actual Base44 backend, via update_entity_schema — a repo commit alone never changes runtime RLS) surfaced that Base44's live RLS engine silently drops any sibling key placed alongside "user_condition" in the same rule object — {"data.school_id": X, "user_condition": Y} evaluates as user_condition ALONE, X is discarded. That shape was already the DEPLOYED form of most tenant-scoping rules across this app (not something 1.7.3 introduced), found via update_entity_schema's own validator while pushing 1.7.3's fix live. Scanned all 32 entities: 29 had it, 84 instances total, almost all on the data.school_id tenant-isolation clause — meaning any user matching the role half of the rule (e.g. data.app_role:ADMIN) could read/write across ALL schools, not just their own, on nearly every entity in the app. Same defect class jospabloh/cateqhub's CLAUDE.md documents finding once in one entity (Parish) with a note it was worth checking elsewhere — this is elsewhere, at much larger scale. Fixed by wrapping every such pair as an explicit {"$and": [{"user_condition":...}, {...rest}]} — semantics preserved exactly, nothing narrowed or widened beyond restoring the intended tenant scoping. Two further live-engine constraints surfaced and fixed while deploying: (1) a nested $or directly inside another $or is not evaluated on WRITE rules (create/update/delete) — "the branch silently matches" — fixed by flattening (read rules tolerate nested $or fine, left as-is); (2) the entity-side built-in record id must be addressed as "id", not "_id" — Classroom/School/Student used "_id" and were rejected on redeploy; renamed. All 29 corrected entities deployed live via the Base44 MCP and re-fetched to confirm. Added a permanent guard for the primary defect: scripts/validate-rls.mjs now flags any rule object mixing user_condition with sibling keys (previously silent — this exact shape passed validate:rls for years since it's syntactically valid Mongo-style implicit-AND, just not how Base44's engine actually evaluates it). No entity field, property, or intended-access rule changed — verified per-entity that `properties`/`required` are byte-identical before/after and every fix is a pure re-expression of the same access the original (broken) rule intended. 276/276 tests pass; scripts/validate-rls.mjs passes clean (32 entities, new check included); lint clean; build succeeds.

architecture.runtime: browser (client-side only; no application server) + Base44 backend functions for privileged mutations
architecture.router: react-router-dom v7 (declarative mode: BrowserRouter/Routes/Route/useNavigate/Link — stable across v6->v7)
architecture.enforcementBoundary: base44 Row-Level Security (entity + field-level RLS) in base44/entities/*.jsonc + service-role backend functions in base44/functions/*
architecture.language: JavaScript / JSX (type-checked via jsconfig); Deno TypeScript for backend functions

assistantSkills.note: The sibling claude-skills repo holds 48 generic Anthropic/Claude authoring skills (pdf, xlsx, brainstorming, math-olympiad, ...). They are assistant tooling used to BUILD Liuma — NOT features of the application, not integrated into it, and not listed in the user manual.

previousBumpRationale_1_7_16: Patch, security/ops: scheduled full-review audit pass. Pre-flight: repo clean, HEAD == origin/main (6ecb2ec), zero open PRs, no secrets in tree. Full verification suite green before touching anything: lint (incl. validate:functions, 9/40), typecheck, build, validate:rls (33 entities), validate:tenant-roles, test (278/278), test:permissions (23/23), release:gate, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities) — matches every check ci-node.yml runs. First real finding: PRODUCTION DEPLOY DRIFT, the same class of gap 1.7.14 fixed six weeks earlier. The checkpoint carrying 1.7.15's own fixes (credit-protection functions and Module 24's User RLS lock) had built successfully on Base44 but last_deployed_at was null — never pushed live. Fixed via the Base44 platform API's POST /deploy, confirmed by content: list_entity_schemas on User shows rls.write:false live, checkpoint git_commit_hash matches main. Redeploying that code let Base44's security scan see it for the first time (its prior 'clean' result predated these files) — a fresh scan surfaced three real findings, all fixed here: (1) guardedEntityWrite wrote body.data's attribution fields (Attendance.recorded_by, DiaryEntry/Homework.teacher_id, Notice.author_id, PaymentRecord.recorded_by) verbatim via its service-role bypass of each entity's own RLS, letting a caller spoof who authored a record — now overridden server-side from the caller's identity on create, stripped on update. (2) CONFIRMED, medium: the PARENT/EVENTO ChargeItem carve-out trusted client-supplied amount/status, letting a parent record their own event fee as already PAID at amount 0 — now derived server-side from the referenced Event's cost_amount/cost_concept/confirmation_deadline. (3) sendNotificationEmail's new_user_pending event allowed any registered user (including ACTIVE profiles) to repeatedly email a school's admins with a self-chosen name/email/role and no rate limit — narrowed to PENDING-only callers, userName/userEmail now checked against the caller's real identity, roleName derived server-side, and made idempotent via new UserProfile.pending_notification_sent_at. (4) notifyParents' diary path had no delivery-idempotency flag (its own comment said so) — replaying a recordId re-mailed parents every time; new DiaryEntry.parents_notified_at closes it, mirroring Attendance.parent_notified. Second, smaller finding: CHANGELOG.md had fallen one release behind package.json/VERSION_CONTROL.json/appConfig.js (already bumped to 1.7.15 with no corresponding entry) — backfilled. deno isn't available in this sandbox; the three edited functions were syntax-checked with a standalone tsc --noResolve pass (no errors beyond expected npm:/Deno-global resolution noise). Re-verified full suite after every fix: lint, typecheck, build, validate:rls, validate:tenant-roles, test (283/283, +5 new), test:permissions, release:gate, npm audit — all pass. No entity RLS create/read/update/delete rule changed — only two new fields (service-role-write-only in practice) and the four function fixes above. See docs/security-audit-2026-09-28.md for the full scan output and the redeploy/rescan verification. CORRECTION (same day, before merge): a Codex review on this PR caught two real regressions in the first version of findings 3 and 4 above. (3) UserProfile.pending_notification_sent_at was a single flag on the pending user's own profile, but sendByEvent calls sendNotificationEmail once per ACTIVE admin recipient -- the first successful send blocked every other admin in the same school from ever being notified; fixed by tracking per-recipient (pending_notification_recipients, an array, rls.write:false). (4) DiaryEntry.parents_notified_at was set after ANY successful send, so a partial failure (some parents' SendEmail calls succeeding, others failing) permanently skipped retrying the failed ones; fixed by tracking per-recipient (notified_parent_emails, rls.write:false) and only retrying recipients not yet in that array. Both reviews also caught that neither new field had rls.write:false, so the pending user / authoring teacher could forge or clear their own idempotency marker via a normal client update -- now locked, matching the User.school_id/app_role pattern from Module 24, plus guardedEntityWrite strips DiaryEntry's two fields from any client patch as defense-in-depth since that function's service-role write bypasses RLS. Re-verified full suite after these corrections: lint, typecheck, build, validate:rls, validate:tenant-roles, test (283/283, one test widened after a false-fail from its own regex window, not a code issue), test:permissions, release:gate, npm audit -- all pass.
